summary: Ad-hoc 'override' approvals do not trigger JIT provisioning — approval webhook actor_type mismatch
description:
Issue summary: When a manager or admin uses the console's ad-hoc 'override' approval button on an internal access request, the approval webhook is emitted but the JIT provisioning service ignores it. Impact: Users remain without temporary roles, blocking access to runbooks and internal dashboards; this has delayed two oncall escalations this week. Environment: prod us-east, observed across multiple clusters. We suspect the approval-service changed the webhook payload actor_type to 'override' during a recent rollout, while the JIT provisioner only accepts 'manager' or 'self_approval' actor_type values.

Observed window: 2026-03-09 21:30+UTC to present.

Expected behavior: Ad-hoc override approvals should result in the same provisioning flow as a standard manager approval and trigger JIT user creation/role grant.

Actual behavior: The approval-service emits a webhook with payload field actor_type: 'override_admin' (or 'override') and the jit-provisioner logs indicate "unrecognized approver_type, ignoring request". No retry is currently scheduled for unrecognized actor_type events.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a new access request from an internal account for 'runbook-edit' in the support-console (account: test.user+req@redwood.ai).
2) From a manager account, click the console 'Approve -> override' button and add a freeform reason.
3) Observe the approval-service outgoing webhook in Audit -> Webhooks (or via /api/webhooks/recent).
4) Check the jit-provisioner logs for an entry matching the request id and look for 'unrecognized approver_type' or discard behavior.
5) Verify the user has not been granted the temporary role in the RBAC table and cannot access the runbook page.

comments: 2026-03-10T09:12 Jared Morales: Investigating logs from approval-service and jit-provisioner. I can reproduce locally by simulating an 'override' approval. Triage to auth team requested.
2026-03-10T10:05 Mitali Rao: Confirmed payload actor_type changed in last deployment (PR #12813). The schema validator in approval-service no longer maps override->manager. Adding SRE to review.
2026-03-11T14:22 Oncall (Slack #internal-access): Two incidents this week where overriding approval blocked triage. Requesting a short-term mitigation (retry or mapping) until fix rolls out.

2026-03-12T11:45 Jared Morales: Temporary mitigation implemented: admin can use Admin Console -> Approvals -> Mark as 'manager_approved' which triggers the accepted actor_type path. Working on a PR to make jit-provisioner accept legacy override values and add a warning rather than drop events.
2026-03-12T16:02 Mitali Rao: Linked PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/approval-service/pull/12947 to restore actor_type mapping. Leaving open for testing in staging first.
investigation_notes: Root cause hypothesis: approval-service rollout changed the actor_type enum to include 'override_admin' without updating consumers. The jit-provisioner has strict validation and drops unknown types rather than treating them as manager approvals.
Reproduced: yes, by performing an 'override' approval in prod feature-flagged console and tailing jit-provisioner logs. Seen at least 3 occurrences tied to different request IDs in the last 48h.

Impact scope: primarily internal admin overrides in prod-us-east; we have not observed this in staging (feature flag off). Estimated ~4-8 requests/day when oncall uses override during emergency escalations.
Observed related code change: PR #12813 in approval-service introduced actor_type change. Related to INT-271500 where webhook schema was adjusted for external audit requirements.

Temporary mitigation options considered: 1) Backfill an actor_type mapping in approval-service to emit 'manager' alongside 'override_admin'. 2) Make jit-provisioner accept additional actor_type values and treat them as manager approvals. 3) Add retry queue for rejected events.
resolution: Workaround applied: Admins can use Admin Console to mark the request as 'manager_approved' which triggers provisioning. Engineering actions: approval-service PR #12947 created to restore legacy actor_type mapping; jit-provisioner patch PR #12952 to accept 'override_admin' as equivalent to 'manager' and to log a warning instead of dropping. Plan: deploy mapping fix to staging for 24h smoke tests, then roll to prod. Follow-up: add automated alert when provisioning events are discarded. Ticket remains In Progress until both PRs are deployed and verified.
